name: manual_f256c7
claim: Perpetua-Tools' own shared-branch Git workflow was dogfooded by concurrent AI coding sessions: multiple sessions worked on the same reviewed branch, where one session's committed fix became another session's starting point through Git state. Do not infer unproven runtime queue, claim/release, heartbeat, or append-only event-folding usage from that evidence unless direct runtime evidence is attached.

decisions.notes: PR #206 (originally a small skill-wrapper salvage) absorbed STM security-pipeline hardening, atomic claim/release fixes, and memory-durability fixes because 4 sibling PRs (#205/#207/#208 plus this one) were being developed by concurrent AI sessions in real time, converging on and occasionally regressing each other's fixes to the same files. Reconciling the final merge required genuine harmonization across 19 conflicted files rather than picking a side -- both lineages had real, different improvements (BEGIN IMMEDIATE + retry defensiveness vs fsync + hash-cross-check crash-consistency) that needed blending, not choosing.
